options.C: It dissolves completely inside the body over a few days
options.D: It greatly reduces the chance of external bacteria entering the wound

explanation: Closed systems keep the drainage contained within sealed tubing and collection bags, making it harder for germs from the outside environment to reach the healing tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h1)

question: According to the Swiss Cheese Model, when does a serious mistake actually reach the patient?

options.A: When a patient refuses to take prescribed medications
options.B: When a single nurse makes a minor mental calculation
options.C: When the holes in all layers of defense align at the same time
options.D: When hospital management removes all safety policies

explanation: Errors usually happen not because of one person, but when multiple safety checks all fail at the exact same time, lining up their gaps. [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h4)

question: As a nurse, why is your role in medication administration so important?

options.A: Prescribing the correct dosage based on lab results
options.B: Manufacturing safe chemical compounds for hospital use
options.C: Acting as the final safety barrier before the drug reaches the patient
options.D: Selling pharmaceutical supplies to hospital wards

explanation: You are the last line of defense! By double-checking the order and the patient right before giving the drug, you catch mistakes that might have slipped through earlier. Great job keeping patients safe! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T5#GNS125_U4_T5_h1)

question: How does good delegation by a nurse leader show empowerment?

options.A: By shifting unwanted administrative paperwork onto junior staff
options.B: By showing trust in the team's ability to handle important clinical tasks
options.C: By forcing staff to work longer shifts without extra pay
options.D: By removing all accountability from the bedside nurse

explanation: When a leader delegates well, they are saying, 'I trust your skills.' It helps junior nurses grow and take ownership of their duties. [learn more](GST321_U1_T14#GST321_U1_T14_h5)

question: A nurse wants to help secondary school girls prevent anemia using local foods. Which tip is the most practical?

options.A: Drink lots of black tea right after every big meal
options.B: Eat sugary snacks between classes for quick energy
options.C: Eat local dark greens, beans, and vitamin C-rich fruits
options.D: Avoid all animal protein and fish products

explanation: Spot on! Local greens and beans give iron, and adding vitamin C (like a squeeze of orange or lemon) helps the body absorb that iron much better! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T010#GNS227_U2_T010_h8)

question: What part of the female reproductive system does a vulval tumour affect?

options.A: The external female genitalia
options.B: The glandular tissue of the cervix
options.C: The inner lining of the fallopian tubes
options.D: The muscular wall of the uterus

explanation: Vulval tumours specifically develop on the external structures of the female genitalia, such as the labia and clitoris. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h1)

question: Why is home health care such an exciting shift in modern nursing?

options.A: It moves professional care from large hospitals back into the community
options.B: It focuses only on domestic chores rather than medical tasks
options.C: It completely replaces the need for doctors and clinics
options.D: It removes all responsibilities from family caregivers

explanation: Spot on! Instead of keeping everyone stuck in hospital wards, home care brings the healing right into the patient's familiar home environment. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T1#GNS324_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why do government health systems often partner with non-governmental agencies?

options.A: Communities prefer private doctors over public nurses
options.B: Ministries of health do not care about rural populations
options.C: Hospitals lack enough space to store modern medicines
options.D: Government facilities face funding limits and personnel shortages

explanation: You got it! Because budgets and staff numbers can be tight, government agencies often need extra hands to reach every corner of the country. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h1)

question: How can community health nurses best fight social stigma against disability?

options.A: By ignoring cultural beliefs entirely without discussion
options.B: By focusing solely on medication management in clinics
options.C: Through patient advocacy and public health education
options.D: By keeping affected individuals hidden safely at home

explanation: Brilliant! Education and speaking up help clear away harmful myths, replacing fear with inclusion and understanding. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h7)

question: A male patient refuses to talk about his anxiety because he was taught men must always be strong. What process caused this?

options.A: Biological mutation
options.B: Genetic inheritance
options.C: Gender socialization
options.D: Physiological adaptation

explanation: Society's cultural messages teach boys early on that showing weakness is wrong. This shapes how adult men handle emotional pain and whether they seek help. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T5#GNS312_U4_T5_h2)

question: What type of lubricant should always be used on a flatus tube before insertion?

options.A: Water-soluble lubricant
options.B: Sterile cooking oil
options.C: Petroleum-based jelly
options.D: Alcohol-based gel

explanation: Water-soluble lubricant is safe for mucous membranes and prevents trauma, unlike petroleum-based products which are harder to clear and can damage tissues. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T11#GNS212_U1_T11_h4)

question: Which life stage has the fastest human growth rate, coming in second right after infancy?

options.A: Adolescence
options.B: Toddlerhood
options.C: Young adulthood
options.D: Middle childhood

explanation: You've got this! Adolescence is well known as the second fastest period of human growth, right behind infancy. Your body is doing amazing things during these teenage years! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T010#GNS227_U2_T010_h1)

question: What is a very common skin problem caused by unmanaged urine leaks over time?

options.A: Incontinence-associated dermatitis
options.B: Chronic skin pigmentation loss
options.C: Diffuse bacterial cellulitis of the face
options.D: Severe subcutaneous fat necrosis

explanation: When urine sits on the skin, it breaks down the natural skin barrier, causing painful redness and irritation called incontinence-associated dermatitis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h8)

question: Why does chronic straining often lead to the development of hemorrhoids?

options.A: It increases pressure on the blood vessels around the anus
options.B: It strips the protective mucous layer off the colon
options.C: It stops the liver from filtering blood properly
options.D: It causes rapid dehydration of the entire body

explanation: Straining forces extra blood into the rectal and anal veins, causing them to swell and form hemorrhoids. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h3)

question: How does poor quality care directly impact women seeking reproductive health services?

options.A: It encourages them to report staff members to management
options.B: It forces them to demand more expensive medications
options.C: It drives them toward unsafe, alternative healthcare sources
options.D: It has no measurable effect on their health-seeking habits

explanation: Unwelcoming environments, rudeness, and poor treatment discourage clients from visiting formal facilities, pushing them to seek help elsewhere. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h1)

question: A newly bereaved family member sits quietly without crying and says everything is fine. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The person is lying to trick the medical staff
options.B: The person lacks any emotional capacity for love
options.C: The person may be experiencing shock or emotional numbing
options.D: The person has already successfully reached full acceptance

explanation: A lack of tears does not always mean peace; it often indicates emotional shock or denial. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h5)

question: What is the main thing that makes a research study 'non-experimental'?

options.A: The researcher does not manipulate the independent variable.
options.B: Random assignment is used for every participant.
options.C: A new treatment is tested against a placebo.
options.D: The study takes place only in a laboratory setting.

explanation: You've got this! In non-experimental studies, we simply watch and record things as they happen naturally, without changing or meddling with anything ourselves. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T8#GNS224_U1_T8_h1)

question: An infant is brought in at exactly 14 weeks for routine immunization. Which vaccines should you expect to give?

options.A: Final infant doses of polio, pentavalent, and pneumococcal
options.B: Yellow fever and initial oral polio vaccine zero
options.C: BCG and first dose of measles
options.D: Only the annual influenza booster shot

explanation: Well done! At 14 weeks, babies complete their final scheduled series of OPV, IPV, pentavalent, and pneumococcal vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h2)

question: An elderly patient starts feeling dizzy and lightheaded during steam therapy. What is your very first nursing action?

options.A: Stop the treatment and remove the inhaler immediately
options.B: Add more boiling water to increase vapor strength
options.C: Leave the room briefly to fetch a doctor
options.D: Encourage the patient to breathe faster and deeper

explanation: Safety comes first! If a patient feels dizzy or faint, halt the procedure right away to keep them safe from injury. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T6#GNS212_U2_T6_h6)

question: What are the main signs that a family caregiver is suffering from severe burnout?

options.A: A sudden desire to pursue advanced nursing degrees
options.B: Exhaustion, resentment, and emotional exhaustion
options.C: Improved physical strength and restful sleep patterns
options.D: Increased energy and excitement for daily tasks

explanation: Caring for others 24/7 is draining. When a caregiver is completely burnt out, they feel emotionally fried, bone-tired, and sometimes overwhelmed with resentment. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T2#GNS324_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to find out about hidden food taboos during a patient assessment?

options.A: Tell the patient that all traditional beliefs are wrong
options.B: Inspect the patient's kitchen without asking permission
options.C: Wait for laboratory tests to reveal all dietary habits
options.D: Ask open-ended questions about family dietary avoidances

explanation: Asking warm, open questions like 'Are there certain foods your family avoids eating?' helps patients open up without feeling judged or defensive. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T016#GNS227_U2_T016_h6)

question: What does a color change on a chemical indicator strip tell you?

options.A: That the autoclave machine needs immediate factory maintenance
options.B: That the instrument set is sterile and safe for immediate surgery
options.C: That every single bacterial spore inside the pack is completely dead
options.D: That the package was exposed to the required physical conditions

explanation: Chemical strips only show that heat or gas reached the outside of the pack. They are a great clue, but not a 100% guarantee of internal sterility! [learn more](GST114_U2_T11#GST114_U2_T11_h6)

question: Why must even experienced registered nurses take part in continuous professional development?

options.A: Experienced nurses tend to forget all basic nursing procedures
options.B: Medical knowledge and clinical techniques continuously evolve over time
options.C: Hospital accreditation boards punish facilities that do not hold daily exams
options.D: New nursing graduates require constant supervision from senior colleagues

explanation: Healthcare changes every day. Even senior nurses need continuous learning to stay sharp and master the newest, safest techniques. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following groups needs special protective measures during research studies?

options.A: Healthy adult nurses working day shifts on the ward
options.B: Vulnerable populations such as children and unconscious patients
options.C: Senior medical doctors leading research teams
options.D: Hospital administrators reviewing the annual budget

explanation: Vulnerable groups need extra safeguards because they might not be fully able to give true voluntary consent on their own. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h8)

question: Why might a doctor order an MRI instead of a standard X-ray for a suspected bone injury?

options.A: To measure the exact electrical activity in the bone
options.B: To determine the amount of calcium in the bloodstream
options.C: To detect hidden stress fractures or soft tissue damage
options.D: To check the patient's resting blood pressure levels

explanation: MRIs excel at showing soft tissues like ligaments, tendons, and hairline cracks that standard X-ray beams often miss. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is the main physical change that happens during embryonic folding?

options.A: The placenta detaches from the uterine wall
options.B: A flat tissue sheet becomes a three-dimensional cylindrical body
options.C: The neural crest cells migrate to the limbs
options.D: The three germ layers separate into distinct organs

explanation: You got it! Folding takes the flat little disc of cells and curves it into a proper 3D, tube-shaped body plan. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T3#GNS121_U6_T3_h6)

question: Why do health programs built on community mobilisation usually last longer than top-down programs?

options.A: Because government nurses supervise every single household daily
options.B: Because the community takes ownership and actively participates in the solutions
options.C: Because traditional beliefs are completely ignored by the project
options.D: Because foreign donors provide unlimited financial support forever

explanation: When people are part of creating the solution, they care for it and maintain it long after external workers leave. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why does a low rate of childhood immunization help keep an endemic disease active in a community?

options.A: It leaves enough susceptible individuals for the infection to keep spreading
options.B: It forces the infectious agent to change into a non-harmful bacteria
options.C: It improves the environmental conditions for vector breeding grounds
options.D: It eliminates the natural reservoir hosts living inside the community

explanation: When fewer children are vaccinated, the germ easily finds new, unprotected bodies to infect, keeping the transmission cycle alive. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h5)

question: Which of these is a true feature of a polysynaptic reflex arc?

options.A: Total absence of a sensory neuron component
options.B: Presence of one or more interneurons
options.C: Involvement of only a single chemical synapse
options.D: Speed that is always faster than monosynaptic reflexes

explanation: Poly means many! These reflexes use one or more interneurons to handle slightly more detailed tasks, creating a few more connections along the path. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T25#GNS211_U3_T25_h6)

question: A patient's abdominal surgical wound suddenly pops open and loop of bowel peeks out. What is your immediate action?

options.A: Apply an ice pack to the exposed tissue to reduce swelling
options.B: Wait until the scheduled doctor appointment next week to report it
options.C: Cover the area with sterile saline-moistened dressings and call for emergency help
options.D: Gently push the bowel back inside the abdomen and tape it shut

explanation: This is an emergency called evisceration! Keep the organs moist with sterile saline dressings and call for emergency help right away—never push them back in. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h5)

question: A peanut allergy patient feels completely fine 30 minutes after getting epinephrine and asks to go home immediately. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Perform allergy skin prick testing before allowing the patient to leave
options.B: Explain that prolonged observation is required to watch for secondary symptom flare-ups
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately with a prescription for oral antihistamines
options.D: Administer a second dose of epinephrine just to prevent any future problems

explanation: Don't let them rush off just yet! Because of the risk of biphasic reactions, patients need to stay in the hospital for observation for a few hours. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is an example of paralanguage during a patient interaction?

options.A: The medical diagnosis written on a chart
options.B: The physical distance between you and the bed
options.C: The volume and speed of your voice
options.D: The hand gestures used while explaining a procedure

explanation: Paralanguage refers to vocal qualities like pitch, speed, and volume that accompany spoken words. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h1)

question: What is a major reason why clients sometimes stop using modern contraceptives early?

options.A: Sudden nationwide shortages of barrier supplies
options.B: Automatic expiration of contraceptive efficacy after one month
options.C: Anxiety and fear regarding normal physiological side effects
options.D: Mandatory government limits on the duration of use

explanation: Spot on! Many clients stop using a method when they notice minor changes like spotting simply because nobody warned them it's a normal body reaction. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h5)

question: Why does keeping adolescent girls in school help reduce the rate of child marriage?

options.A: It makes them legally immune from all traditional family rules
options.B: It automatically provides their families with monthly government stipends
options.C: It bans them from ever participating in cultural ceremonies
options.D: It raises their aspirations, builds skills, and delays early union

explanation: Education empowers girls with knowledge and future prospects, making early marriage less likely and less desirable. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h7)

question: In males, which organ sits right below the bladder and wraps around the urethra?

options.A: The epididymis
options.B: The prostate gland
options.C: The testicle
options.D: The seminal vesicle

explanation: The prostate gland wraps like a ring around the upper male urethra. This is why an enlarged prostate in older men can make it hard to pass urine! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T1#GNS213_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the main meaning of 'food insecurity'?

options.A: Temporary fasting practiced during religious or cultural holiday seasons
options.B: A personal choice to go on a strict weight-loss diet for health reasons
options.C: Lack of consistent access to enough safe and nutritious food for a healthy life
options.D: Having too many grocery stores in a single neighborhood community

explanation: Food insecurity means a person or family never quite knows where their next wholesome meal is coming from. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T027#GNS227_U2_T027_h6)

question: What is the best nursing action when a dying patient talks about spiritual distress?

options.A: Prescribe an antidepressant medication immediately
options.B: Listen empathetically and offer to arrange a chaplain visit
options.C: Argue theological points to prove the patient wrong
options.D: Tell the patient not to worry about religious matters

explanation: Wonderful! As nurses, we support spiritual needs by being a caring listener and connecting patients with someone who can offer the right spiritual comfort. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a problem caused by severe maternal anaemia for the unborn baby?

options.A: Fetal hypoxia and distress
options.B: Intrauterine growth restriction
options.C: Preterm birth and low birth weight
options.D: Macrosomia and high birth weight

explanation: You got it! Anaemia starves the baby of oxygen and nutrients, leading to low birth weight or growth restriction—never a giant baby (macrosomia). [learn more](GNS226_U2_T020#GNS226_U2_T020_h6)

question: What is the typical normal oxygen saturation range for a healthy adult breathing room air?
explanation: Healthy individuals without lung or heart disease usually maintain oxygen saturation levels between 95% and 100%. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the main goal of respecting patient autonomy in end-of-life care?

options.A: Reducing the workload of the attending nursing staff
options.B: Ensuring family members make all major medical decisions
options.C: Allowing the patient to keep control over their choices
options.D: Speeding up the discharge process from the facility

explanation: Respecting autonomy means empowering the patient to direct their own care and make meaningful decisions about their remaining time. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h2)

question: Which part of the eye is damaged in all types of glaucoma?

options.A: The outer cornea
options.B: The crystalline lens
options.C: The optic nerve
options.D: The white of the eye

explanation: Glaucoma is all about pressure or stress hurting the optic nerve fibers, which slowly creates blind spots if left untreated. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T3#GNS311_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which hormone acts like a chill pill for the uterus, keeping its muscles calm and preventing early contractions?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Estrogen

explanation: You got it! Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles, keeping the uterus nice and quiet throughout the pregnancy journey. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h5)

question: Why are pregnant women and young children grouped together as a special population?

options.A: They take up most of the housing budget
options.B: They do not pay any community taxes by law
options.C: They share unique health vulnerabilities and face high risks of preventable illness
options.D: They are required to stay in the hospital continuously

explanation: Spot on! Mothers and young kids go through sensitive stages of life where quick, targeted health support can prevent major illnesses. They're a top priority in community nursing! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T26#GNS225_U5_T26_h1)

question: Why is ethical data management particularly critical in nursing research?

options.A: Because it prevents frequency tables from having errors
options.B: Because computers cannot process named data without codes
options.C: Because nursing data involves sensitive personal health information
options.D: Because ethical clearance replaces the need for data cleaning

explanation: Healthcare records are deeply private, and nurses have an ethical duty to safeguard patient confidentiality throughout every step of data organization. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h8)

question: Why can a very long fallopian tube lead to difficulty getting pregnant?

options.A: The fertilized egg may not reach the uterus in time
options.B: The ovaries stop making eggs from stretching
options.C: The cervix closes up to block sperm
options.D: The uterus rejects incoming hormones

explanation: If the journey takes too long, the embryo might implant in the wrong spot or stop growing before it reaches the uterus. Every question makes you a better nurse! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h3)

question: How does neural control of hormones differ from humoral control?

options.A: Neural control takes hours to respond compared to fast humoral pathways
options.B: Neural control relies entirely on negative feedback loops in the liver
options.C: Neural control uses direct nerve impulses rather than blood metabolite monitoring
options.D: Neural control only regulates reproductive organs instead of metabolic ones

explanation: Neural means nerves sending direct electrical messages, while humoral means the gland is checking chemicals floating in the blood. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T6#GNS211_U1_T6_h3)

question: How do deep, widespread fungal infections often show up in lung tissue scans?

options.A: As watery blisters covering the outer skin layer
options.B: As acute pus-filled abscesses with rapid cell rupture
options.C: As a gray pseudomembrane blocking the trachea
options.D: As granulomatous lesions that resemble tuberculosis

explanation: Fungi love to form granulomas in the lungs just like TB does, which can sometimes make them tricky to tell apart on an X-ray! [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h8)

question: What major physical change happens inside the brain during late-stage GPI?

options.A: Nerve fibers rapidly grow too thick and strong.
options.B: Brain tissue shrinks and nerve cells are lost.
options.C: Pus and fluid swell up inside the ventricles.
options.D: Fatty plaques build up in large clumps.

explanation: You nailed it! Long-term inflammation slowly destroys brain cells, leading to a noticeable shrinking of the brain known as cerebral atrophy. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T1#GNS222_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is a key role of a nurse acting as a community champion for reproductive health?

options.A: Writing national health insurance budget laws
options.B: Replacing traditional village chiefs in council meetings
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical contraceptive drugs
options.D: Educating and advocating outside hospital walls

explanation: Community champions extend their reach into local spaces to educate populations and advocate for better health practices. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h6)

question: What is the name of the suture that separates the two parietal bones along the top of the fetal head?

options.A: Sagittal suture
options.B: Coronal suture
options.C: Frontal suture
options.D: Lambdoidal suture

explanation: The sagittal suture runs right along the midline at the top of the head, dividing the left and right parietal bones. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h1)

question: Which chemical substance is primarily responsible for causing uterine contractions and pain in dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Adrenaline
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Prostaglandins

explanation: Prostaglandins build up in the uterine lining and stimulate strong contractions of the uterine muscle, leading to cramping pain. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which organ in the body is the main workstation for breaking down most medications?

options.A: The stomach
options.B: The kidneys
options.C: The liver
options.D: The pancreas

explanation: The liver is like the body's chemical factory. It uses special enzymes (the famous cytochrome P450 system) to process and break down most of the drugs we take. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T4#GNS215_U2_T4_h2)

question: A patient reports waking up three times every night to pass urine. What term should the nurse document?

options.A: Enuresis
options.B: Nocturia
options.C: Polyuria
options.D: Oliguria

explanation: Nocturia specifically refers to interrupted sleep caused by the need to void during the night. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which activity is commonly included in the daily routine of a half-way house?

options.A: Intensive major surgery training workshops
options.B: Strict solitary confinement in locked rooms
options.C: Mandatory bed rest for twenty-four hours
options.D: Shared morning chores and group meetings

explanation: Spot on! Daily schedules feature teamwork activities like shared chores and meetings to encourage social interaction and cooperation. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h5)

question: Within how many hours must a single unit of packed red blood cells be completely infused?

options.A: Twelve hours
options.B: Four hours
options.C: Thirty minutes
options.D: Twenty-four hours

explanation: Keep an eye on the clock! Blood must finish within four hours so bacteria don't start multiplying in room temperature. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T18#GNS122_U1_T18_h5)

question: What crucial details must always be included on a community health referral form?

options.A: The financial salary grade of the attending nurse
options.B: The personal home phone number of the village chief
options.C: Assessment findings and initial care given
options.D: A complete inventory of clinic furniture

explanation: You got it! The receiving hospital needs to know your assessment findings and what emergency treatments you already started before they arrived. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T13#GNS225_U2_T13_h6)

question: What do we call infections that take advantage of a weakened immune system?

options.A: Opportunistic infections
options.B: Secondary autoimmune conditions
options.C: Nosocomial infections
options.D: Primary bacterial sepsis

explanation: Spot on! These are germs that a healthy immune system easily handles, but they 'seize the opportunity' when defenses are low. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h7)

question: A patient getting ready for discharge is worried about taking her pain pills right. What should you do first?

options.A: Tell the patient not to worry because pain is all in the mind
options.B: Cancel the prescription and give only herbal remedies instead
options.C: Ask a family member to manage all medication doses at home
options.D: Review the medication schedule slowly and check for understanding

explanation: Taking a little extra time to walk through the dosing schedule ensures the patient feels confident and safe at home. Excellent patient advocacy! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h6)

question: During a clinic visit, a husband answers every question for his quiet wife, and she won't make eye contact. What should you suspect?

options.A: An imbalance in power and communication within the family
options.B: The hospital waiting room is curing her anxiety
options.C: The wife has perfect physical and mental health
options.D: The couple communicates like absolute experts

explanation: Pay attention to body language! When one person always speaks for another, it often points to a power imbalance or fear holding the quieter partner back. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which hormone from the pituitary gland triggers ovulation right in the middle of the cycle?

options.A: Luteinizing hormone
options.B: Thyroid-stimulating hormone
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Think 'LH surge!' A sudden spike in Luteinizing Hormone (LH) is the exact trigger that causes the ovary to release the egg. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h4)

question: Why is a severe lack of vitamin B1 (thiamine) a major worry in hyperemesis?

options.A: It directly causes sudden gestational diabetes in the second trimester
options.B: It triggers immediate placental abruption and severe bleeding
options.C: It can lead to serious neurological issues like Wernicke's encephalopathy
options.D: It stops the production of amniotic fluid completely

explanation: Starvation and vomiting deplete vitamin B1, which can trigger confusion and nerve issues known as Wernicke's encephalopathy. Knowing this helps you protect your patients early! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h4)

question: What event finally tells the secondary oocyte to finish its second division?

options.A: Entry of a sperm cell
options.B: Degeneration of the corpus luteum
options.C: Arrival in the uterus
options.D: A drop in progesterone levels

explanation: Brilliant! The egg waits patiently in the fallopian tube, and the moment a sperm enters, it completes its final cell division. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h6)

question: Which group is usually eligible for DRF exemptions in our hospitals?

options.A: Elected political office holders
options.B: Employed corporate executives
options.C: Wealthy private business owners
options.D: Indigent elderly patients without support

explanation: Older adults who lack pensions or family financial backup are standard beneficiaries of these hospital welfare safety nets. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h3)

question: In many communities, which group faces a high risk from improperly disposed medical waste due to scavenging at dump sites?

options.A: Informal waste pickers and scavengers
options.B: Hospital administrative office managers
options.C: Licensed medical equipment vendors
options.D: Senior medical consultants and surgeons

explanation: That's right. People who sort through open municipal dumps to find reusable items often run into discarded needles and toxic waste without any protective gear. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h5)

question: Why are visual aids and practical demonstrations useful during health counseling in primary care?

options.A: They replace the need for the nurse to speak at all
options.B: They make health messages easier to understand for people with varying literacy levels
options.C: They ensure patients never forget a single word of advice
options.D: They make the clinic look more modern and well-equipped

explanation: Visuals and demonstrations bridge literacy gaps and make abstract health concepts concrete and memorable. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h6)

question: Why must you wait for the alcohol on the skin to dry before sticking the patient?

options.A: To activate the antiseptic properties of the alcohol
options.B: To ensure the skin surface becomes completely sterile
options.C: To make the outer skin layers easier to pierce
options.D: To prevent stinging and burning sensations upon entry

explanation: Patience pays off! If the alcohol isn't dry, the needle drags it down into the tissue, causing a sharp, unnecessary sting for your patient. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is the main goal of palliative care?

options.A: To speed up the dying process
options.B: To cure the underlying disease
options.C: To provide long-term rehabilitation therapy
options.D: To improve quality of life for patients and families

explanation: You've got this! Palliative care is all about bringing comfort, easing pain, and making life as good as possible for patients and their loved ones, rather than trying to cure the illness. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of a macronutrient that the body needs in large amounts?

options.A: Trace minerals
options.B: Iron supplements
options.C: Vitamins
options.D: Carbohydrates

explanation: Correct! 'Macro' means big—carbs, proteins, and fats are the big-ticket items our bodies need daily in large quantities for fuel. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h4)

question: Why do we bother grouping research studies into different types?

options.A: To make every clinical trial take less time to finish
options.B: To make reading journals and finding study types easier
options.C: To ensure that all patients receive the exact same treatment
options.D: To increase the financial funding for the hospital

explanation: You've got this! Grouping research designs simply helps nurses quickly understand how a study was done and what kind of evidence it brings to the table. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h1)

question: A patient with severe dehydration is expected to show which kidney response regulated by hormones?

options.A: Low levels of ADH leading to dilute, high-volume urine
options.B: Massive secretion of sodium and water into the distal tubule
options.C: High levels of ADH leading to concentrated, low-volume urine
options.D: Complete stoppage of all tubular reabsorption in the cortex

explanation: Dehydration stimulates the release of ADH, causing the kidneys to conserve water and produce small amounts of very concentrated urine. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h8)

question: During wound healing, which cell type rushes in to build new collagen and repair the tissue matrix?

options.A: Keratinocytes
options.B: Mast cells
options.C: Melanocytes
options.D: Fibroblasts

explanation: Fibroblasts are the master builders of healing skin! They migrate into wounds during the repair phase to pump out fresh collagen and rebuild the tissue. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h7)

question: When handling a wet plaster cast, why should nurses use the palms of their hands instead of their fingertips?

options.A: To stop the wet plaster material from sticking permanently to skin
options.B: To prevent indentations that can cause pressure sores on the skin
options.C: To prevent the nurse from getting skin irritation from chemicals
options.D: To make sure the heavy cast does not crack before it dries

explanation: Fingertips leave deep dents in wet plaster. Those little flat spots can press painfully against the skin and cause pressure ulcers later. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h5)

question: What is the single most reliable way to monitor daily changes in a patient's fluid balance?

options.A: Daily body weight measurement
options.B: Counting how many times they eat
options.C: Measuring abdominal girth
options.D: Checking skin turgor on the arm

explanation: One liter of fluid weighs one kilogram, making daily weights the fastest and most accurate indicator of gain or loss. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h6)

question: Why is proper labeling crucial when taking skin snips from different body parts of the same patient?

options.A: To speed up the microscope staining process safely
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of laboratory processing
options.C: To determine how much local anesthetic was injected
options.D: To track which anatomical site yielded the parasites

explanation: Spot on! Parasite concentration can differ across body sites, so knowing the exact spot helps doctors measure how heavy the infection is. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent cross-contamination in the fridge?

options.A: Storing raw meat on the top shelf above fresh vegetables
options.B: Cleaning refrigerator shelves regularly with sanitizer
options.C: Keeping raw poultry separate from ready-to-eat salads
options.D: Using tightly sealed containers for all raw animal products

explanation: Never put raw meat on top! Juices can drip down onto your veggies, causing nasty contamination. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h6)

question: How do standard daily contraceptive pills primarily prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By permanently blocking the fallopian tubes with scar tissue
options.B: By stopping ovulation and changing the cervical mucus
options.C: By killing all bacteria inside the vaginal canal
options.D: By neutralizing stomach acid so hormones cannot absorb

explanation: The hormones in the pill do a double-duty job: they tell the body to pause ovulation and make the cervical mucus thick so sperm can't get through. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which animal is the main natural home for the Lassa fever virus here in Nigeria?

options.A: The domestic dog
options.B: Freshwater snails
options.C: The multimammate rat
options.D: Free-roaming cattle

explanation: Great job! The multimammate rat sheds the Lassa virus in its waste, which can easily contaminate food items in our homes and barns. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which skin-dwelling cell releases histamine when an early inflammation or allergy starts?

options.A: Melanocytes
options.B: Adipocytes
options.C: Mast cells
options.D: Keratinocytes

explanation: Mast cells hold onto histamine and release it when triggered, which kickstarts blood flow and swelling during an inflammatory response. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h2)

question: Which of these is a major warning sign of severe dehydration in a sick child?

options.A: Flushed skin that feels hot to the touch
options.B: An unusually loud and constant cry
options.C: Swelling in both lower legs and feet
options.D: Lethargy or unconsciousness with sunken eyes

explanation: When a child is severely dehydrated, they lose so much fluid that they become very weak, drowsy, or even unconscious, with noticeably sunken eyes. This is an emergency! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h3)

question: Why must used needles be placed immediately into a hard, puncture-proof container?

options.A: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries to staff
options.B: To prevent patients from stealing the metal needles
options.C: To make it easier for the cleaning crew to burn them
options.D: To comply with hospital fashion and sorting rules

explanation: Puncture-proof sharps containers stop sharp needles from poking through soft plastic bags and injuring nurses or housekeepers. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h3)

question: How does active immunization protect the body against future infections?

options.A: By destroying all existing white blood cells in the bloodstream
options.B: By transferring ready-made antibodies directly from another person
options.C: By stimulating the immune system to produce its own antibodies
options.D: By providing instant chemical disinfection on the skin surface

explanation: Active immunity acts like a gym workout for your immune system, teaching it to build its own antibodies and remember germs for later. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h5)

question: Which item should be counted as part of a patient's fluid intake?

options.A: An intramuscular pain injection
options.B: An intravenous blood transfusion
options.C: A solid tablet pain medication
options.D: A dry solid piece of toast

explanation: Blood products and IV fluids introduce liquid directly into the vascular system and must be counted as intake. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h3)

question: Which needle size and length is standard for an adult intramuscular injection?

options.A: 25 gauge, 1/2 inch needle
options.B: 27 gauge, 3/8 inch needle
options.C: 22 gauge, 1.5 inch needle
options.D: 31 gauge, 5/8 inch needle

explanation: You need a longer needle and a wider opening (like a 22-gauge, 1.5-inch) to bypass skin and fat and reach deep down into adult muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h3)

question: A clinic nurse wants to stop teenage girls from dropping out of school due to menstrual hygiene challenges. What is the most practical community action?

options.A: Advise all young girls to stay home during their menstrual periods
options.B: Provide free sanitary pads and educate both girls and community members on menstrual management
options.C: Report the affected families to the federal ministry of education for neglect
options.D: Recommend that local schools close down entirely during rainy seasons

explanation: Providing pads and open education removes the shame and practical barriers that make girls miss school. Simple solutions go a long way in public health! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T5#GNS225_U5_T5_h7)

question: Which of these is the most common type of cancerous vulval tumour?

options.A: Basal cell skin carcinoma
options.B: Primary vulval melanoma
options.C: Squamous cell carcinoma
options.D: Bartholin gland adenocarcinoma

explanation: Correct! Squamous cell carcinoma makes up the vast majority of malignant vulval growths you will see in practice. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h2)

question: What is the primary job of the large intestine in the human body?

options.A: Digesting complex fats and proteins
options.B: Filtering waste products out of the blood stream
options.C: Producing most of the body's digestive enzymes
options.D: Absorbing water and forming stool

explanation: The main function of the colon is to take liquid chyme from the small intestine, absorb the water and electrolytes, and turn it into solid feces. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h1)

question: A patient on chemo for bone sarcoma has a temperature of 38.5°C and chills. What is your priority nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to put on a heavy sweater and drink hot tea
options.B: Administer a dose of routine oral pain medication for the chills
options.C: Notify the healthcare provider immediately for potential neutropenic sepsis
options.D: Document the finding in the chart and recheck the temperature in six hours

explanation: Chemo lowers white blood cells, making fever a true medical emergency. Always report it right away to protect your patient from sepsis! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T19#GNS222_U1_T19_h6)

question: Why must you NEVER use a tongue depressor to check the throat of a child you suspect has acute epiglottitis?

options.A: It causes severe pain in the gums
options.B: It interferes with accurate pulse oximetry
options.C: It can trigger sudden total airway closure
options.D: It makes the fever spike higher immediately

question: Among these clinical situations, which one calls for cold therapy instead of heat?

options.B: Generalized joint ache from morning arthritis
options.C: A tense muscle spasm in the upper shoulder
options.D: Chronic lower back stiffness in an older adult

question: A community health nurse wants to build strong herd immunity against a viral illness in a local village. What should be the top priority?

options.A: Distributing vitamin supplements
options.B: Isolating all healthy children indoors
options.C: Testing local water supplies for bacteria
options.D: Mass vaccination campaigns

explanation: Brilliant! Mass vaccination builds a protective shield around the whole community, making it almost impossible for the virus to find a new victim. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T2#GNS313_U1_T2_h7)

question: How is thiamine usually given during an acute crisis of Wernicke encephalopathy?

options.C: Rubbed onto the skin as a lotion
options.D: Mixed into cold fruit juice

question: What is the proper way to disconnect an electrical appliance from the wall?

question: How can clinical nurses positively influence waste management practices on their wards?

options.C: By buying new incineration machines for the hospital
options.D: By acting as role models and teaching junior staff correct sorting

question: Why can it be tricky for nurses to spot clinical depression in physically disabled patients?

options.A: Physical therapists handle all mental health evaluations

options.C: Patients with disabilities are legally barred from taking antidepressants
options.D: Symptoms like fatigue and sleep changes can overlap with physical illness

question: What is the main danger of health workers assuming they know what the community needs best?

options.C: It forces local leaders to step down from their positions

question: In reproductive health, what does the abbreviation mCPR stand for?

options.B: Modern Contraceptive Prevalence Rate
options.C: Monthly Clinical Patient Record
options.D: Maternal Child Protection Ratio

question: What is the medical name for nearsightedness?

options.A: Hyperopia

question: Which major electrolyte hangs out mostly INSIDE our body cells (the intracellular fluid)?

question: What is wound dehiscence?

question: What delayed complication of a sting can show up days later with fever, joint pain, and a skin rash?

question: What should a nurse do immediately after finding abnormal, life-threatening changes during an exam?

question: What is a vector in the context of disease transmission?

options.C: A drug resistant bacterial strain found in hospital wards
options.D: A contaminated hospital instrument used on multiple patients

explanation: Vectors are living carriers like mosquitoes, ticks, or fleas that transfer infectious agents from one animal or human to another. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of palliative care in a long-term care setting?

options.A: Curing the underlying chronic terminal disease
options.B: Eliminating the need for family involvement
options.C: Accelerating the physical dying process safely
options.D: Relieving pain and managing distressing symptoms

question: What is the main goal of public health policies in government?

options.A: To stop foreign doctors from visiting

options.C: To guide resource distribution and structure healthcare delivery
options.D: To make huge profits for drug manufacturing companies

question: How do optical sensors in regular fitness wristbands usually measure your heart rate?

options.D: By calculating body temperature shifts on the wrist

question: In clinical nursing, how do we truly know how much pain a patient is in?

options.C: Pain is a psychological illusion created by anxiety.

question: How should a nurse respond to a patient who admits to using traditional herbal remedies?

options.A: By threatening to discharge the patient immediately from the hospital

options.C: With an open, non-judgmental attitude to encourage honest communication
options.D: By laughing at the remedies to show they have no scientific value

question: Which of these is a serious danger sign in pregnancy that means 'go to the clinic now'?

options.D: Mild morning nausea during the first trimester

question: Why do oral medications have to pass through the liver before reaching the rest of the body?

options.A: The liver is the primary site where red blood cells absorb the drug

options.C: Bile salts are required to activate every type of oral pill
options.D: Hepatic first-pass metabolism alters or breaks down part of the drug

question: Why must pit latrines be constructed a safe distance away from community drinking wells?

options.A: To prevent underground waste seepage from contaminating the drinking water
options.B: To ensure the toilets receive enough direct sunlight
options.C: To keep the water source smelling fresh and perfumed
options.D: To make it harder for children to play near the toilets

question: When it comes to formatting your paper, what golden rule connects your in-text citations and reference list?

options.A: Every in-text citation must match an entry in the reference list

options.C: References must be completely different from the in-text citations
options.D: References should be listed in alphabetical order without citations

question: Which home modification is most helpful for preventing bathroom falls?

options.C: Using dim lighting to avoid harsh glares
options.D: Keeping the bathroom door locked at night

question: A nurse notices that outsourced lab staff keep missing deadlines, which delays patient medications. What is the best step for the nurse?

options.A: Perform all laboratory tests independently in addition to standard nursing duties
options.B: Ignore the delays because outsourced staff are outside the nursing department's control
options.C: Advise patients to purchase private insurance to get faster lab results
options.D: Document the delays and report them through proper administrative channels for contract review

explanation: As a patient advocate, document the facts clearly and report them up the administrative chain so management can fix the vendor issue. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h8)

question: Why should a nurse view medication administration protocols as a safety net?

options.A: They catch potential mistakes before the drug reaches the patient

options.D: They prevent the pharmacy from ever making a dispensing mistake

explanation: Protocols act as multi-layered checks that intercept errors originating from prescribing, dispensing, or preparation stages. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h1)

question: A healthy traveler returns from an area with an Ebola outbreak. Public health officials tell them to stay home and check their temperature daily for 21 days. What is this called?

question: In public health, what do we mean by 'vulnerable populations'?

options.C: Groups with a higher risk of poor health due to disadvantages
options.D: Wealthy citizens who travel abroad for routine medical checkups

explanation: Vulnerable groups—like pregnant mothers, infants, or the very poor—face extra hurdles that make it easier for them to fall sick. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h5)

question: Why must nurses assess the mental well-being of people undergoing quarantine?

options.A: Depression causes immediate immunity to infections
options.B: Mental illness stops the incubation period of viruses
options.C: Psychological stress lowers body temperature
options.D: Confinement often leads to anxiety, stress, and frustration

question: What is the most important thing to watch out for after a patient has their chest tube removed?

options.A: Mild redness around the edges of the healed skin suture line

options.C: Signs of breathing difficulty or the chest problem returning
options.D: Temporary soreness at the chest site when coughing

question: Why are progestin-only pills usually recommended for breastfeeding mothers instead of combined oral pills?

options.A: They provide permanent protection after a single dose
options.B: They do not interfere with breast milk production
options.C: They completely stop all menstrual bleeding forever
options.D: They protect the mother against sexually transmitted infections

question: Roughly what percentage of raw sewage is actually water?

options.B: Less than 10 percent

options.D: Exactly 50 percent

question: Why do community rumors about birth control often spread faster than clinical facts?

options.A: Doctors teach these rumors during nursing school
options.B: They travel easily through trusted word-of-mouth networks
options.C: The government pays people to broadcast them on radio
options.D: They are printed inside official hospital textbooks

explanation: Spot on! People naturally trust informal chats with neighbors and friends, which is why unverified stories spread so quickly. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T006#GNS226_U6_T006_h4)

question: How do hospitals keep imaging going during sudden power outages?

options.A: Utilizing backup generators and battery-powered portable units
options.B: Performing manual sketches of internal organs at the bedside
options.C: Canceling all diagnostic imaging tests for the entire week
options.D: Waiting indefinitely until the public electricity grid restores power

explanation: Backup generators and portable machines are lifesavers when the main power grid goes down in clinical settings. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical environmental challenge for home health nurses?

options.A: Navigating unfamiliar neighborhoods during community visits
options.B: Cluttered walkways and poor lighting inside private residences
options.C: Managing biohazardous waste disposal without hospital utility rooms
options.D: Guaranteed 24-hour security guards stationed outside the front door

explanation: Home care nurses do not have personal security guards stationed at every home visit; environmental risks are often unpredictable. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h6)

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive method?

options.A: A subdermal hormonal implant
options.B: A packet of daily oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Spermicidal foam applied before sex
options.D: Male latex condoms used during intercourse

explanation: Implants and intrauterine devices are classified as LARC methods because they work continuously for years without daily action from the user. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)

question: How do gallstones usually start forming inside the biliary system?

options.A: Chemical imbalances causing solid particles to form in the bile
options.B: Calcium deposits traveling up from the small intestine
options.C: Excess protein buildup in the liver ducts
options.D: Infection spreading from the pancreas

explanation: You've got this! Stones start forming when components in bile, like cholesterol and bilirubin, become imbalanced and clump together. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T6#GNS222_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of the watery fluid and mucus secreted inside the small intestine?

options.A: To pump hydrochloric acid into the bloodstream
options.B: To lubricate contents and protect the tissue lining
options.C: To produce hormones that control appetite
options.D: To store bile until fats arrive in the diet

explanation: Think of mucus and fluid as a slippery shield; they keep food moving smoothly while protecting the delicate intestinal walls from irritation. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h6)

question: Which structures should you palpate when doing a routine male genital check?

options.A: Testes and epididymis
options.B: Bulbourethral glands only
options.C: Ureters and renal pelvis
options.D: Seminal vesicles and bladder

explanation: You got it! Gently checking the testes and the epididymis helps you spot any lumps, swelling, or tenderness early on. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is collaboration with traditional birth attendants and local volunteers important for a PHC nurse?

options.A: It eliminates the need for government-supplied medications
options.B: It ensures that traditional workers stop practicing completely
options.C: It fosters teamwork and bridges traditional practices with formal health services
options.D: It allows the nurse to transfer all clinical responsibilities to volunteers

explanation: Collaborating with local groups helps guide traditional practices safely and encourages mothers to seek formal care. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h7)

question: What is the single best way to stop resistant germs from spreading between patients?

options.A: Keeping patient room windows completely sealed shut
options.B: Administering daily multivitamins to all visitors
options.C: Sprinkling chemical disinfectants on hospital floors hourly
options.D: Performing thorough hand hygiene before and after care

explanation: Never underestimate simple handwashing! It remains our number one defense against carrying germs from patient to patient. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T18#GNS313_U1_T18_h7)

question: A patient with terrible watery diarrhea has raw, red skin around their bottom. What is the best immediate nursing care?

options.A: Apply a drying powder to absorb moisture and stop wiping
options.B: Scrub the irritated skin firmly with soap and a rough cloth
options.C: Leave the skin exposed to room air without any protection
options.D: Clean the area gently, dry it, and apply a barrier cream

explanation: You got it! Liquid stool is harsh on the skin. Clean gently and use a good barrier cream to protect raw areas from irritation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of preventive nutrition counselling?

options.A: Reviewing individual hospital charts for acute surgical patients
options.B: Prescribing medications to cure advanced infectious diseases
options.C: Stopping health problems before they start in healthy populations
options.D: Treating severe kidney failure with emergency dialysis diets

explanation: Preventive counselling aims to keep healthy people healthy through smart food choices and risk reduction education. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h5)
